text:
Dear Partners,

The quarter closed the way a good harvest does—steady, unhurried, and better than the worrying suggested it might be. The central bank held its policy rate at 4.50%, inflation came in at 2.4%, and high-yield spreads settled at 320bps, tight enough to tell you the market is not pricing in much trouble. Equities extended their gains, up +4.0% for the quarter, and new issuance windows have reopened across the calendar—always a welcome sign, like seeing the barn doors swing open again after a long winter of caution.

We think of this business the way a good tenant farmer thinks of the land he works: you don't own it outright, but you tend it like you do, because the harvest depends on the relationship, not just the paperwork. That's the spirit behind every position in this book. Our NAV index sits at 106.0, and we posted a quarterly return of +3.2%, bringing us to +6.0% year-to-date and +45.0% since inception. We're pleased with these marks, and we want to be candid about what sits behind them: senior secured paper, first in line, protected by the structural seniority that has always been the backbone of how we underwrite. That seniority doesn't just sound good in a letter—it's the reason we sleep at night when spreads tighten and issuance reopens all at once, because tight markets can make everyone feel like a genius, and we'd rather be boring and protected.

On the handful of names still working through amendments first flagged last quarter, conversations remain constructive. Borrowers and sponsors alike understand that a covenant reset done right preserves value for everyone at the table—that's the partnership talking, not the contract. We continue to work these situations the way we'd want a lender to work with us: patiently, with eyes open, favoring solutions that keep enterprises funded and our capital senior.

Looking ahead, we remain constructive, though not naively so. Reopened issuance windows and tightening spreads are good news, but good news has a way of inviting complacency, and we'd rather stay a step ahead of that than a step behind it. Should credit conditions turn—and we are not forecasting that they will—the same structural seniority that protects us today would be doing the heavy lifting then too. We think that protection is durable, though not without risk. We also think it's prudent to keep watching the pace of new issuance for signs that underwriting discipline could be loosening market-wide, even as our own book holds firm.

As always, we're grateful for the trust of our limited partners, and for the diligence of our advisors in keeping us honest. We'll keep tending the land.

With appreciation,
The Firm
